newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key points of Japan penalties against DKB, Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Key points of Japan penalties against DKB, Nomura.

text.p: Following are the key points of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) administrative penalties announced on Wednesday against Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd for their involvement in a racketeer payoff scandal.
PENALTIES AGAINST NOMURA:
*Halt of its own-account stock-related dealing, including options and index trading, from August 6 to December 31.
*Suspension of its stock-related business at all branches from August 6 to August 12.
*Suspension of securities trading and securities futures broking at the first corporate division at Nomura's headquarters from August 6 to December 5.
*Suspension of the head office as a whole, excluding the first corporate division, from securities trading and securities futures broking from August 6 to September 5.
*Ban on participation in the auction and underwriting of public bonds, including Japanese government bonds (JGBs), municipal bonds and government-guaranteed bonds, from August 6 to December 31.
MOF also ordered Nomura to draw up a report by September 19 that would:
*Clarify responsibilities at Nomura
*Identify steps Nomura will take to strengthen internal management structures
*Identify steps to improve staff compliance with laws and regulations
*Provide a review of trading operations within the company
*Clarify responsibility for actions at Nomura which made it difficult for facts to surface
*Identify steps Nomura will take to cut ties with "anti-social forces", including sokaiya.
PENALTIES AGAINST DKB :

*Suspension of new loan business, except for key housing loans, from August 6 until December 31. New corporate loans will be prohibited completely as well as those for individuals, except for housing loans.
The suspension does not include lending by overseas branches.

*Extension of a ban on its participation in auctions and underwriting public bonds, including Japanese government bonds (JBGs), municipal bonds and government-guaranteed bonds, until the end of this year.
*Suspension from opening new branches or offices either domestically or overseas from August 6 until August 5, 1998.
*Ban on conducting sales of investment trusts at its branches, making use of holding companies, or liquidating assets by new methods from August 6 until August 5, 1998.
MOF also ordered DKB to draw up a report by September 19 that would:
*Identify steps the bank will take to strengthen internal controls
*Identify steps it will take to cut ties with "anti-social forces", including sokaiya.
*Introduce a third party to follow up on whether the bank was actually carrying out measures to strengthen its internal supervision.
